as one executable. It reads Markdown on standard input and writes HTML on standard output.\n\n## Usage\n\n```sh\n./commonmark < document.md > document.html\nprintf '# Hello\\n' | ./commonmark\n```\n\n## Interface\n\n- **Input (stdin):** UTF-8 Markdown. Invalid UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD. LF, CR, and CRLF are all line endings. U+0000 is replaced with U+FFFD.\n- **Output (stdout):** rendered HTML only, encoded as UTF-8.\n- **Diagnostics (stderr):** used only for internal errors.\n- **Arguments:** none. The executable takes no options.\n- **Exit status:** always 0, for any input, including empty input.\n\n## Requirements\n\nPython 3.11 or later. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WaUPUuZhGFY1diKF9UR7p8","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\n\n    A final line ending terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one, so the one empty\n    entry that `split_lines` leaves after it is dropped. Otherwise an unclosed fenced code block would\n    gain a blank line.\n    \"\"\"\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines = lines[:-1]\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n----\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_atx_headings.py\ntest_autolinks.py\ntest_backslash_escapes.py\ntest_block_engine.py\ntest_blocks.py\ntest_code_spans.py\ntest_emphasis.py\ntest_entities.py\ntest_executable.py\ntest_fenced_code.py\ntest_foundation.py\ntest_html_blocks.py\ntest_images.py\ntest_indented_code.py\ntest_line_breaks.py\ntest_link_reference_definitions.py\ntest_links.py\ntest_raw_html.py\ntest_render.py\ntest_thematic_breaks.py\n\"\"\"Block-engine acceptance and end-to-end tests: paragraphs, blank lines, and HTML escaping through\nthe `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe four declared checks from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md are transcribed first, with their\nassertions unchanged. The remaining tests compare the exact stdout bytes, which is the state\nthe executable hands back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_engine_paragraph_count(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Blank-line-separated paragraphs render as one p element each.\"\"\"\n    paragraphs = [\"alpha beta\", \"gamma delta\", \"epsilon\"]\n    source = \"\\n\\n\".join(paragraphs) + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"</p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    for text in paragraphs:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_multiline_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Consecutive non-blank lines with arbitrary indentation after the first stay in one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    first = \"first line\"\n    second = \"second line\"\n    third = \"third line\"\n    source = first + \"\\n\" + \"             \" + second + \"\\n\" + third + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    for text in (first, second, third):\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_blank_lines_ignored(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Leading, trailing and repeated blank lines add no blocks; a blank-only document gives no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    word = \"content\"\n    padded = \"\\n  \\n\\n\" + word + \"\\n\\n\\n  \\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, padded)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n    blank = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\")\n    assert blank.returncode == 0\n    assert blank.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_engine_html_escaping(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Special characters in paragraph text are escaped, so only the paragraph tags contribute angle brackets.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\">\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"hello world\\n\").stdout == \"<p>hello world</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_two_paragraphs_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"dc6e74a2-7d1d-4ee1-8b1d-06f37ec31205","uuid":"b4d41abf-663f-4b95-bf3a-9edb24181c06","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:44:24.466Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n\"\"\"Process I/O boundary for the `commonmark` executable.\n\nResponsibility: read raw bytes from `sys.stdin.buffer`, decode UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement,\nnormalize line endings, replace U+0000, and write HTML to `sys.stdout.buffer`. Diagnostics go to\n`sys.stderr` only, and the exit status is 0 for every input.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks, inlines, render\n\nREPLACEMENT_CHARACTER = \"�\"\nLINE_ENDING_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n|\\r|\\n\")\n\n\ndef decode_source(data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Decode raw input bytes as UTF-8, replacing each invalid byte with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    return data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n\ndef split_lines(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split text on LF, CR, or CRLF, and replace each U+0000 with U+FFFD.\"\"\"\n    text = text.replace(\"\\x00\", REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER)\n    return LINE_ENDING_PATTERN.split(text)\n\n\ndef render_lines(lines: list[str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Parse the lines into a block tree and return the HTML document.\n\n    A final line ending terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one, so the one empty\n    entry that `split_lines` leaves after it is dropped. Otherwise an unclosed fenced code block would\n    gain a blank line.\n    \"\"\"\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines = lines[:-1]\n    root = blocks.parse_lines(lines)\n    return render.render_document(root, lambda raw: inlines.parse_inline(raw, root.references))\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Run the executable: stdin Markdown to stdout HTML. Always returns 0.\"\"\"\n    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()\n    try:\n        lines = split_lines(decode_source(data))\n        html = render_lines(lines)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"commonmark: internal error: {exc!r}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        html = \"\"\n    sys.stdout.buffer.write(html.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    sys.stdout.buffer.flush()\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n----\n__pycache__\nconftest.py\ntest_atx_headings.py\ntest_autolinks.py\ntest_backslash_escapes.py\ntest_block_engine.py\ntest_blocks.py\ntest_code_spans.py\ntest_emphasis.py\ntest_entities.py\ntest_executable.py\ntest_fenced_code.py\ntest_foundation.py\ntest_html_blocks.py\ntest_images.py\ntest_indented_code.py\ntest_line_breaks.py\ntest_link_reference_definitions.py\ntest_links.py\ntest_raw_html.py\ntest_render.py\ntest_thematic_breaks.py\n\"\"\"Block-engine acceptance and end-to-end tests: paragraphs, blank lines, and HTML escaping through\nthe `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe four declared checks from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md are transcribed first, with their\nassertions unchanged. The remaining tests compare the exact stdout bytes, which is the state\nthe executable hands back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Engine.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_engine_paragraph_count(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Blank-line-separated paragraphs render as one p element each.\"\"\"\n    paragraphs = [\"alpha beta\", \"gamma delta\", \"epsilon\"]\n    source = \"\\n\\n\".join(paragraphs) + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"</p>\") == len(paragraphs)\n    for text in paragraphs:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_multiline_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Consecutive non-blank lines with arbitrary indentation after the first stay in one paragraph.\"\"\"\n    first = \"first line\"\n    second = \"second line\"\n    third = \"third line\"\n    source = first + \"\\n\" + \"             \" + second + \"\\n\" + third + \"\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n    for text in (first, second, third):\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_engine_blank_lines_ignored(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Leading, trailing and repeated blank lines add no blocks; a blank-only document gives no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    word = \"content\"\n    padded = \"\\n  \\n\\n\" + word + \"\\n\\n\\n  \\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, padded)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n    blank = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n \\n\\t\\n\")\n    assert blank.returncode == 0\n    assert blank.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_engine_html_escaping(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Special characters in paragraph text are escaped, so only the paragraph tags contribute angle brackets.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"x < y > z & w\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\">\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_paragraph_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"hello world\\n\").stdout == \"<p>hello world</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_two_paragraphs_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01WaUPUuZhGFY1diKF9UR7p8","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n48\t        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n49\t        end += 1\n50\t    return end_col - col\n51\t\n52\t\n53\tclass Cursor:\n54\t    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n55\t\n56\t    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n57\t        self.line = line\n58\t        self.pos = 0\n59\t        self.col = 0\n60\t\n61\t    @property\n62\t    def rest(self) -> str:\n63\t        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n64\t        return return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n70\t\n71\t    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n72\t        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n91\t\n92\t    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n93\t        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n94\t\n95\t        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n96\t        \"\"\"\n97\t        target = self.col + columns\n98\t        while self.pos < len(self.line) and    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n105\t\n106\t    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n107\t        self.kind = kind\n108\t        self.parent: Block | None = None\n109\t        self.children: list[Block] = []\n110\t        self.is_open = True\n111\t        self.lines: list[str] = []\n112\t        self.content = \"\"\n113\t        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. otherwise None.\"\"\"\n124\t        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n125\t            return self.children[-1]\n126\t        return None\n127\t\n128\t\n129\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n130\tclass BlockType:\n131\t    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n132\t\n133\t    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. accepts_lines: bool = False\n142\t    interruptible: bool = False\n143\t    lazy: bool = False\n144\t    start: StartRule | None = None\n145\t    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n146\t bool:\n189\t    return False\n190\t\n191\t\n192\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\n193\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n194\t\n195\t\n196\tdef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n197\t    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n198\t\n199\t    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n200\t    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n201\t    \"\"\"\n202\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n203\t        return None\n204\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n205\t    line = cursor.line\n206\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n207\t        return None\n208\t    marker = line[start]\n209\t    count = 0\n210\t    for char in line[start:]:\n211\t        if char == marker:\n212\t            count += 1\n213\t        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n214\t            return None\n215\t    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n216\t        return None\n217\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n218\t    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n219\t\n220\t\n221\tATX_MARKER = \"#\"\n222\tATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n223\t\n224\t\n225\tdef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n226\t    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n227\t\n228\t    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n229\t    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n230\t    \"\"\"\n231\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n232\t        return None\n233\t    line = cursor.line\n234\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n235\t    end = start\n236\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n237\t        end += 1\n238\t    level = end - start\n239\t    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n240\t        return None\n241\t    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n242\t        return None\n243\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n244\t    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n245\t    heading.level = level\n246\t    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n247\t    return heading\n248\t\n249\t\n250\tdef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n251\t    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n252\t\n253\t    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n254\t    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n255\t    \"\"\"\n256\t    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n257\t    if stripped == content:\n258\t        return content\n259\t    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n260\t        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n261\t    return content\n262\t\n263\t\n264\tDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\n265\tPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n266\t    \"paragraph\",\n267\t    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n268\t    accepts_lines=True,\n269\t    interruptible=True,\n270\t    lazy=True,\n271\t    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n272\t    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n273\t)\n274\t# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n275\t# as soon as the next line arrives.\n276\tTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n277\t    \"thematic_break\",\n278\t    continues=_never_continues,\n279\t    start=_thematic_break_start,\n280\t)\n281\t# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. start=_atx_heading_start,\n287\t)\n288\t\n289\t\n290\tCODE_INDENT = 4\n291\t\n292\t\n293\tdef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n294\t    \"\"\"Start an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n298\t    \"\"\"\n299\t    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n300\t        return None\n301\t    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n302\t    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n303\t\n304\t\n305\tdef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n306\t    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n307\t\n308\t    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n309\t    \"\"\"\n310\t    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n311\t        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n312\t        return True\n313\t    return up to that many are removed from\n351\t    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n352\t    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n353\t    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n354\t    \"\"\"\n355\t\n356\t    char: str\n357\t    length: int\n358\t    indent: int\n359\t    language: str\n360\t    opening: bool = True\n361\t    closed: bool = False\n362\t\n363\t\n364\tdef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n365\t    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n366\t    end = start\n367\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n368\t        end += 1\n369\t    return end\n370\t\n371\t\n372\tdef _language(info: str) -> str:\n373\t    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n374\t    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n375\t    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n376\t\n377\t\n378\tdef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n379\t    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n380\t\n381\t    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n382\t    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n383\t    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n384\t    \"\"\"\n385\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n386\t        return None\n387\t    line = cursor.line\n388\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n389\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n390\t        return None\n391\t    char = line[start]\n392\t    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n393\t    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n394\t        return None\n395\t    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n396\t    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n397\t        return None\n398\t    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n399\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n400\t    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n401\t    block.fence = fence\n402\t    return block\n403\t\n404\t\n405\tdef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n406\t    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n407\t\n408\t    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n409\t    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n410\t    \"\"\"\n411\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n412\t        return False\n413\t    line = cursor.line\n414\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n415\t    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n416\t    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n417\t\n418\t\n419\tdef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n420\t    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n421\t\n422\t    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n423\t    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n424\t    \"\"\"\n425\t    fence = block.fence\n426\t    assert fence is not None\n427\t    if fence.closed:\n428\t        return False\n429\t    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n430\t        fence.closed = True\n431\t        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n432\t        return True\n433\t    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n434\t    return True\n435\t\n436\t\n437\tdef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n438\t    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n# container.\nFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"fenced_code\",\n    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_fenced_code_start,\n    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nHTML_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\nHTML_ATTRIBUTE = (\n    r\"[ \\t]+[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n    r\"(?:[ \\t]*=[ \\t]*(?:[^\\\"'=<>`\\x00-\\x20]+|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"))?\"\n)\n# A complete open tag or closing tag, with its name captured, as the raw HTML grammar defines it. \\t>]|$)\", re.IGNORECASE)\nRAW_TEXT_END = re.compile(r\"</(?:pre|script|style|textarea)>\", re.IGNORECASE)\n# Start condition 6 names, matched case-insensitively.\nBLOCK_TAG_NAMES = (\n    \"address\", \"article\", \"aside\", \"base\", \"basefont\", \"blockquote\", \"body\", \"caption\", \"center\",\n    \"col\", \"colgroup\", \"dd\", \"details\", \"dialog\", \"dir\", \"div\", \"dl\", \"dt\", \"fieldset\", \"figcaption\",\n    \"figure\", \"footer\", \"form\", \"frame\", \"frameset\", \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"head\",\n    \"header\", \"hr\", \"html\",   return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert registry.register(PARAGRAPH)\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_start_rules_are_the_thematic_break_atx_heading_indented_fenced_and_html() -> None:\n    assert blocks.DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts() == (\n _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.startswith(\"<<\"):\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RAW)\n    return None\n\n\nRAW = BlockType(\n    \"raw\",\n    continues=lambda block, cursor: True,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    add_line=lambda block, cursor: block.lines.append(cursor.rest),\n    start=_raw_start,\n)\n\n\ndef test_start_rule_is_not_tried_inside_a_non_interruptible_leaf() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, root.children[0].lines[-1] == \"***\"\n\n\n# --- Lazy paragraph continuation, via a test-only container ---\n\n\ndef _quote_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    index = None\n\n\nQUOTE = BlockType(\"quote\", continues=_quote_continues, is_container=True, start=_quote_start)\n\n\ndef quote_registry() -> BlockRegistry:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(QUOTE)\n    return registry\n\n\ndef test_quote_holds_its_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"> b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_the_lazy_continuation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"\", \"b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\", \"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"a\", \"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.startswith(\"<<\"):\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RAW)\n    return None\n\n\nRAW = BlockType(\n    \"raw\",\n    continues=lambda block, cursor: True,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    add_line=lambda block, cursor: block.lines.append(cursor.rest),\n    start=_raw_start,\n)\n\n\ndef test_start_rule_is_not_tried_inside_a_non_interruptible_leaf() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RAW)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"<<\", \"***\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"raw\"]\n    assert root.children[0].lines[-1] == \"***\"\n\n\n# --- Lazy paragraph continuation, via a test-only container ---\n\n\ndef _quote_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    index = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if cursor.line[index : index + 1] == \">\":\n        cursor.advance_to(index + 1)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _quote_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    index = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if cursor.line[index : index + 1] == \">\":\n        cursor.advance_to(index + 1)\n        return Block(QUOTE)\n    return None\n\n\nQUOTE = BlockType(\"quote\", continues=_quote_continues, is_container=True, start=_quote_start)\n\n\ndef quote_registry() -> BlockRegistry:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(QUOTE)\n    return registry\n\n\ndef test_quote_holds_its_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"> b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_unmarked_line_is_a_lazy_continuation_of_the_quote_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_the_lazy_continuation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", \"\", \"b\"], quote_registry())\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.advance_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    char = line[start]\n    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n        return None\n    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n        return None\n    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n    block.fence = fence\n    return block\n\n\ndef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n\n    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return False\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n\n    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.opening:\n        fence.opening = False\n        return\n    if fence.closed:\n        return\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n\n    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n    \"\"\"\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n\n\n# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n# container.\nFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"fenced_code\",\n    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_fenced_code_start,\n    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nHTML_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\nHTML_ATTRIBUTE = (\n    r\"[ \\t]+[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n    r\"(?:[ \\t]*=[ \\t]*(?:[^\\\"'=<>`\\x00-\\x20]+|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"))?\"\n)\n# A complete open tag or closing tag, with its name captured, as the raw HTML grammar defines it. Only\n# spaces and tabs may follow it on the line.\nCOMPLETE_OPEN_TAG = re.compile(rf\"<({HTML_TAG_NAME})(?:{HTML_ATTRIBUTE})*[ \\t]*/?>[ \\t]*\")\nCOMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG = re.compile(rf\"</({HTML_TAG_NAME})[ \\t]*>[ \\t]*\")\n# Start condition 1 names. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds. A line that\n        # can only lazily continue the open paragraph may start only a block that can interrupt one.\n        cursor.lazy_paragraph = not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and self._tip().kind.lazy\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                cursor.lazy_paragraph = False\n                self._close_below(container)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers.
