Type 7 cannot start while a paragraph is open, which\n    is the case when the container takes lines or the line lazily continues the open paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    text = cursor.rest.lstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    for kind in HTML_KINDS:\n        if not kind.can_interrupt and (container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph):\n            continue","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    char = line[start]\n    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n        return None\n    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n        return None\n    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n    block.fence = fence\n    return block\n\n\ndef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n\n    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return False\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n\n    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.opening:\n        fence.opening = False\n        return\n    if fence.closed:\n        return\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n\n    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n    \"\"\"\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n\n\n# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n# container.\nFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"fenced_code\",\n    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_fenced_code_start,\n    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nHTML_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\nHTML_ATTRIBUTE = (\n    r\"[ \\t]+[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n    r\"(?:[ \\t]*=[ \\t]*(?:[^\\\"'=<>`\\x00-\\x20]+|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"))?\"\n)\n# A complete open tag or closing tag, with its name captured, as the raw HTML grammar defines it. Only\n# spaces and tabs may follow it on the line.\nCOMPLETE_OPEN_TAG = re.compile(rf\"<({HTML_TAG_NAME})(?:{HTML_ATTRIBUTE})*[ \\t]*/?>[ \\t]*\")\nCOMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG = re.compile(rf\"</({HTML_TAG_NAME})[ \\t]*>[ \\t]*\")\n# Start condition 1 names. Type 7 excludes them, because type 1 owns them.\nRAW_TEXT_TAG_NAMES = frozenset((\"pre\", \"script\", \"style\", \"textarea\"))\nRAW_TEXT_START = re.compile(r\"<(?:pre|script|style|textarea)(?=[ \\t>]|$)\", re.IGNORECASE)\nRAW_TEXT_END = re.compile(r\"</(?:pre|script|style|textarea)>\", re.IGNORECASE)\n# Start condition 6 names, matched case-insensitively.\nBLOCK_TAG_NAMES = (\n    \"address\", \"article\", \"aside\", \"base\", \"basefont\", \"blockquote\", \"body\", \"caption\", \"center\",\n    \"col\", \"colgroup\", \"dd\", \"details\", \"dialog\", \"dir\", \"div\", \"dl\", Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Returns","+    False and leaves the cursor untouched when the line has no marker.","+    \"\"\"","+    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:","+        return False","+    marker = cursor.next_nonspace()","+    if marker == len(cursor.line) or cursor.line[marker] != BLOCK_QUOTE_MARKER:","+        return False","+    cursor.advance_to(marker + 1)","+    cursor.consume_columns(1)","+    return True","+","+","+def _block_quote_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:","+    \"\"\"A line continues the quote when it has a marker. A line without one is left to the lazy rule.\"\"\"","+    return _consume_block_quote_marker(cursor)","+","+","+def _block_quote_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:","+    \"\"\"Start a block quote when the line opens with a `>` marker.\"\"\"","+    if not _consume_block_quote_marker(cursor):","+        return None","+    return Block(BLOCK_QUOTE)","+","+","+# A block quote is a container. A line without a marker still reaches a paragraph inside the quote","+# through the engine's lazy rule, and any other unmatched block closes.","+BLOCK_QUOTE = BlockType(","+    \"block_quote\",","+    continues=_block_quote_continues,","+    is_container=True,","+    start=_block_quote_start,","+)","+","+"," class BlockRegistry:","     \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01D7iN4jYxYBaLF86F48kKiH","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"dc6e74a2-7d1d-4ee1-8b1d-06f37ec31205","uuid":"2bffbe3b-3682-4124-9223-092c96d93b1f","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:48:59.384Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(HTML_BLOCK)\n","newString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(HTML_BLOCK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(BLOCK_QUOTE)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KDCRQaJAguU7AZZ1jL9foV","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"dc6e74a2-7d1d-4ee1-8b1d-06f37ec31205","uuid":"30f730f2-6ba2-49fc-ba17-02c400898a4a","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:49:02.905Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","oldString":"def render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":","newString":"def render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _render_children(root, parse_inline)\n\n\ndef _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"block_quote\":\n        return f\"<blockquote>\\n{_render_children(block, parse_inline)}</blockquote>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":","originalFile":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in root.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":58,"oldLines":10,"newStart":58,"newLines":16,"lines":["     `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1mBBPLLHeCDMRuV85wx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Fn27Zu5fo4Yx7XAKAi6kiW","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_block_quotes.py","content":"\"\"\"Block quote tests: the eight declared checks from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md, then block-tree, cursor\nand exact-output tests for marker handling, lazy continuation and the blank-line rule.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import BLOCK_QUOTE, DEFAULT_REGISTRY, PARAGRAPH, Block, Cursor, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_quote_basic_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> # Foo\\n> bar\\n> baz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_space_optional(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    for source in (\"># Foo\\n>bar\\n\", \"   > # Foo\\n   > bar\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_lazy_continuation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> bar\\nbaz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_nested_lazy(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > > foo\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 3\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_blank_line_separates(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    separated = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\\n> bar\\n\")\n    joined = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert separated.returncode == 0\n    assert joined.returncode == 0\n    assert separated.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 2\n    assert joined.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_quote_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_no_lazy_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \">     foo\\n    bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_quote_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_quote_marker_only_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_renders_nothing(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"\").stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_nested_quotes_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_marker_only_line_keeps_one_quote_and_splits_paragraphs(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n>\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n<p>bar</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_quote_and_following_text_is_a_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n<p>bar</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_with_leading_indent_of_three_spaces_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"   > foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_with_tab_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    # The tab after the marker is one column of the optional space; its other three columns are text\n    # indentation that the paragraph strips.\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\tfoo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_partly_consumed_tab_leaves_columns_as_code_indentation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    # `>` takes one column, the first tab takes two more, and the second tab keeps two columns of\n    # indentation under the four-column code rule.\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\t\\tfoo\\n\").stdout == (\n        \"<blockquote>\\n<pre><code>  foo\\n</code></pre>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_quote_content_after_no_optional_space_keeps_text(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Block tree ---\n\n\ndef test_marker_creates_a_block_quote_holding_its_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\"]\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_includes_block_quote() -> None:\n    assert BLOCK_QUOTE in DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts()\n\n\ndef test_two_marked_lines_form_one_quote() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_closes_the_quote_before_the_next_marked_line() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"block_quote\"]\n    assert [paragraph_texts(child) for child in root.children] == [[\"foo\"], [\"bar\"]]\n\n\ndef test_quote_closes_at_end_of_input_and_is_finalized() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\"])\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef test_quote_may_be_entered_from_a_paragraph_without_a_blank_line() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\", \"bar\"]\n\n\ndef test_quote_contents_do_not_reach_the_parent_paragraph_after_a_blank() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"\", \"bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root.children[0]) == [\"foo\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\", \"bar\"]\n\n\ndef test_nested_quote_nests_in_the_tree() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > > foo\"])\n    depth = 0\n    node = root\n    while node.children and node.children[0].kind is BLOCK_QUOTE:\n        node = node.children[0]\n        depth += 1\n    assert depth == 3\n    assert kinds(node) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_empty_quote_has_no_children() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\">\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert root.children[0].children == []\n\n\n# --- Lazy continuation: only paragraph text may continue a quote without a marker ---\n\n\ndef test_lazy_line_joins_the_paragraph_inside_a_nested_quote() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_heading_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"# bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"atx_heading\"]\n\n\ndef test_thematic_break_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"***\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"thematic_break\"]\n\n\ndef test_fence_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"```\", \"bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"fenced_code\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\"]\n\n\ndef test_indented_code_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \" test_quote_nested_lazy(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > > foo\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 3\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_blank_line_separates(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    separated = assert separated.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 2\n    assert joined.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_quote_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert The rest of the first tab and the second tab\n    # give six columns of indentation; the code rule takes four, leaving two spaces.","originalFile":"\"\"\"Block quote tests: the eight declared checks from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md, then block-tree, cursor\nand exact-output tests for marker handling, lazy continuation and the blank-line rule.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import BLOCK_QUOTE, DEFAULT_REGISTRY, PARAGRAPH, Block, Cursor, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_quote_basic_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> # Foo\\n> bar\\n> baz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_space_optional(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    for source in (\"># Foo\\n>bar\\n\", \"   > # Foo\\n   > bar\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_lazy_continuation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> bar\\nbaz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_nested_lazy(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > > foo\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import BLOCK_QUOTE, DEFAULT_REGISTRY, PARAGRAPH, Block, Cursor, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_quote_basic_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> # Foo\\n> bar\\n> baz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_space_optional(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    for source in (\"># Foo\\n>bar\\n\", \"   > # Foo\\n   > bar\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_lazy_continuation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> bar\\nbaz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_nested_lazy(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > > foo\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 3\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_blank_line_separates(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    separated = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\\n> bar\\n\")\n    joined = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert separated.returncode == 0\n    assert joined.returncode == 0\n    assert separated.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 2\n    assert joined.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_quote_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_no_lazy_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \">     foo\\n    bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the executable ---\n\n\ndef test_single_quote_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_quote_marker_only_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_renders_nothing(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"\").stdout == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_nested_quotes_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_marker_only_line_keeps_one_quote_and_splits_paragraphs(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n>\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n<p>bar</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_quote_and_following_text_is_a_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n<p>bar</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_with_leading_indent_of_three_spaces_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"   > foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_with_tab_output_is_exact(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    # The tab after the marker is one column of the optional space; its other three columns are text\n    # indentation that the paragraph strips.\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\tfoo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_quote_partly_consumed_tab_leaves_columns_as_code_indentation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    # `>` and one column of the first tab form the marker. The rest of the first tab and the second tab\n    # give six columns of indentation; the code rule takes four, leaving two spaces.\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">\\t\\tfoo\\n\").stdout == (\n        \"<blockquote>\\n<pre><code>  foo\\n</code></pre>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n    )\n\n\ndef test_quote_content_after_no_optional_space_keeps_text(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \">foo\\n\").stdout == \"<blockquote>\\n<p>foo</p>\\n</blockquote>\\n\"\n\n\n# --- Block tree ---\n\n\ndef test_marker_creates_a_block_quote_holding_its_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\"]\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_includes_block_quote() -> None:\n    assert BLOCK_QUOTE in DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts()\n\n\ndef test_two_marked_lines_form_one_quote() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_closes_the_quote_before_the_next_marked_line() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"block_quote\"]\n    assert [paragraph_texts(child) for child in root.children] == [[\"foo\"], [\"bar\"]]\n\n\ndef test_quote_closes_at_end_of_input_and_is_finalized() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\"])\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef test_quote_may_be_entered_from_a_paragraph_without_a_blank_line() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\", \"bar\"]\n\n\ndef test_quote_contents_do_not_reach_the_parent_paragraph_after_a_blank() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"\", \"bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root.children[0]) == [\"foo\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\", \"bar\"]\n\n\ndef test_nested_quote_nests_in_the_tree() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > > foo\"])\n    depth = 0\n    node = root\n    while node.children and node.children[0].kind is BLOCK_QUOTE:\n        node = node.children[0]\n        depth += 1\n    assert depth == 3\n    assert kinds(node) == [\"paragraph\"]\n\n\ndef test_empty_quote_has_no_children() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\">\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert root.children[0].children == []\n\n\n# --- Lazy continuation: only paragraph text may continue a quote without a marker ---\n\n\ndef test_lazy_line_joins_the_paragraph_inside_a_nested_quote() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > foo\", \"> bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert kinds(root.children[0]) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_heading_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"# bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"atx_heading\"]\n\n\ndef test_thematic_break_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"***\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"thematic_break\"]\n\n\ndef test_fence_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"```\", \"bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"fenced_code\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\"]\n\n\ndef test_indented_code_does_not_continue_a_quote_lazily() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"    bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_indented_line_is_lazy_paragraph_text_not_code() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"    bar\"])\n    assert \"indented_code\" not in kinds(root)\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\"]\n\n\ndef test_type_seven_html_does_not_interrupt_a_lazy_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", '<a href=\"x\">'])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == ['foo\\n<a href=\"x\">']\n\n\ndef test_type_six_html_interrupts_a_quote_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> foo\", \"<div>\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"html_block\"]\n\n\ndef test_lazy_continuation_follows_the_deepest_open_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > foo\", \"bar\", \"baz\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\\nbar\\nbaz\"]\n\n\ndef test_lazy_line_after_a_closed_inner_block_is_not_lazy() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> # foo\", \"bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"block_quote\", \"paragraph\"]\n\n\n# --- Cursor: column-aware consumption of a tab that is only partly taken ---\n\n\ndef test_consume_columns_splits_a_straddling_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.consume_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.pos == 0\n    assert cursor.col == 2\n    assert cursor.rest == \"  x\"\n\n\ndef test_consume_columns_finishes_a_split_tab_on_the_next_consumption() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.consume_columns(2)\n    cursor.consume_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.pos == 1\n    assert cursor.col == 4\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_consume_columns_takes_a_whole_tab_that_fits() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.consume_columns(4)\n    assert cursor.pos == 1\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_consume_columns_takes_plain_spaces_one_column_each() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"   x\")\n    cursor.consume_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \" x\"\n\n\ndef test_consume_columns_stops_at_text() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"a  b\")\n    cursor.consume_columns(3)\n    assert cursor.pos == 0\n    assert cursor.rest == \"a The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import BLOCK_QUOTE, DEFAULT_REGISTRY, PARAGRAPH, Block, Cursor, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_quote_basic_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> # Foo\\n> bar\\n> baz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_marker_space_optional(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    for source in (\"># Foo\\n>bar\\n\", \"   > # Foo\\n   > bar\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_lazy_continuation(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> bar\\nbaz\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_nested_lazy(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> > > foo\\nbar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n\\n> bar\\n\")\n    joined = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert separated.returncode == 0\n    assert joined.returncode == 0\n    assert separated.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 2\n    assert joined.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_quote_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"foo\\n> bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_quote_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"    > foo\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert    foo\\n    bar\\n\")\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 2\n\n\n# --- Exact output through the test_nested_quote_nests_in_the_tree() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> > > foo\"])\n    depth = 0\n    node = root\n    while node.children and node.children[0].kind is BLOCK_QUOTE:\n        node test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_pads_a_tab_after_spaces_to_the_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"  \\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_two_tabs_as_eight() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_not_blank_with_text() -> None:\n    assert not Cursor(\"  a\").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_nonspace_tracks_column_across_a_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"  \\t x\")\n cursor.advance_to(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"c\"\n\n\n# --- Empty and blank input ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([]).children == []\n\n\ndef blocks.ATX_HEADING,\n        blocks.INDENTED_CODE,\n        blocks.FENCED_CODE,\n        blocks.HTML_BLOCK,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_lazy_block_type_must_accept_lines() -> None:\n    with _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"a\", \"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.startswith(\"<<\"):\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n
